title: Image scanning and supply-chain security
description: Scan Docker images for vulnerabilities, verify image provenance with signatures, and build a supply-chain security pipeline for production deployments.

data.text: Container supply-chain security is the practice of ensuring that the code, dependencies, base images, and build pipelines that produce a container image are trustworthy. It covers vulnerability scanning, image signing, provenance attestation, and admission control at deploy time.

A vulnerability scanner compares the packages in a container image against a database of known vulnerabilities. Scanners such as Trivy, Grype, and Snyk can run locally, in CI, or as part of your container registry. The goal is to catch known CVEs before the image reaches production.

data.title: Scanning an image with Trivy
data.content: Run Trivy against a local image to list critical and high vulnerabilities.

data.text: Not every CVE is exploitable in your image. A vulnerability in a package that is not installed, or in a package that is installed but not reachable from the network, may not be a practical risk. Use context-aware triage rather than blindly blocking every CVE above a threshold.

An image that passes vulnerability scanning is still not necessarily safe. It could have been built from a compromised source, modified after scanning, or replaced with a look-alike image in the registry. Image signing and provenance attestation address these risks by cryptographically binding an image to the build that produced it.

data.title: Key supply-chain security concepts
items: Docker Content Trust (DCT) signs images with Sigstore cosign and verifies signatures before pull
SLSA provenance attestations record the build source, builder, and dependencies in a signed attestation
Notation is a CNCF project for signing and verifying container images with multiple signatures and standards
Sigstore provides free code signing certificates and a transparency log for supply-chain artifacts

data.title: Signing an image with cosign
data.content: Sign a pushed image with a key pair and verify it before deployment.
data.code:
# Sign the image
cosign sign --key cosign.key myregistry.example.com/myapp:1.0.0

# Verify the signature before deployment
cosign verify --key cosign.pub myregistry.example.com/myapp:1.0.0 \
  --certificate-identity myapp-builder \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://accounts.google.com

data.text: A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is a machine-readable inventory of every component in an image. Syft, Trivy, and Docker Scout can generate SBOMs in CycloneDX or SPDX format. SBOMs let you answer the question 'what is actually inside this image' without rebuilding or scanning it.

data.title: Generating an SBOM with Syft
data.content: Generate a CycloneDX SBOM for a local image.

data.text: Automate scanning, signing, and SBOM generation in your CI/CD pipeline so that every image is checked before it can be deployed. Deny images that fail scanning, lack a signature, or have an unexpected SBOM fingerprint.

data.title: CI/CD supply-chain gate
data.content: A simplified pipeline step that blocks images with critical vulnerabilities.
data.code:
steps:
  - name: Build image
    run: docker build -t myapp:${{\github.sha}} .

  - name: Scan image
    run: |
      trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL myapp:${{\github.sha}}

  - name: Generate SBOM
    run: syft myapp:${{\github.sha}} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

  - name: Sign image
    env:
      COSIGN_PASSWORD: ${{\secrets.COSIGN_PASSWORD}}
    run: |
      echo "${{ secrets.COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY }}" | base64 -d > cosign.key
      cosign sign --key cosign.key myregistry.example.com/myapp:${{\github.sha}}

data.title: Supply-chain attacks are rising
data.text: Attacks such as dependency confusion, typosquatting, and compromised build pipelines have increased dramatically. Scanning alone is not enough. Combine scanning with image signing, SBOM generation, and a trusted build environment.

Docker Scout is Docker's native supply-chain security platform. It integrates with Docker Hub and Docker Desktop to provide vulnerability data, SBOM generation, and policy enforcement directly in the Docker workflow. Scout can also compare images and show you how a new base image version changes your vulnerability profile.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Scan every image before it reaches production with Trivy, Grype, or Snyk
Sign images to prove they were built by your trusted pipeline
Generate SBOMs so you can audit components without rebuilding or rescanning
Automate scanning, signing, and SBOM generation in CI/CD with hard failure gates
Use Docker Scout for integrated visibility into image vulnerabilities and policy compliance
data.takeaway: Supply-chain security is a pipeline discipline: every image must be scanned, signed, and attested before it is allowed to run in production.
